Spread and level base aggregate and sand according to drawings and layout lines.
Cut blocks, bricks, and stone to size with cutting machines.
Lay units one by one in herringbone, basket-weave, and other patterns while leaving expansion joints.
Compact, fill joints, and sweep using tampers and plate compactors.
Install curbs and edge restraints to prevent movement.
Check levelness and slope and repair hollow or loose areas.

paragraphs: At dawn, unload materials and establish layout lines. Spend the morning kneeling to lay blocks and cutting edges with an angle grinder. In the afternoon, repeatedly compact the surface as dust splashes onto your trousers. Toward evening, sweep jointing sand into gaps and settle it with water. Before leaving, lie close to the ground and recheck the slope section by section with a level.

In one sentence: make the ground level and durable. The work includes layout and grading, cutting and laying units, compacting and filling joints, installing curbs, and rechecking slopes. It combines physical labor with disciplined processes and completes hardscape surfaces.
